subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted `/exec` session defaults continue to override later `tools.exec` config, or should operator/global exec security take precedence or clear those stored values after config changes?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the fix changes a documented session-state and security-precedence contract for authorized channel senders.

options.title: Make operator policy authoritative
options.body: Have stricter operator/global exec policy win over stale stored session values, with a tested reset or migration path for existing entries.

options.title: Keep session persistence as documented
options.body: Keep stored `/exec` defaults taking precedence, but document the security tradeoff and provide an operator-friendly way to inspect or clear them.

options.title: Add explicit reset tooling first
options.body: Leave precedence unchanged until a doctor or session-reset path can safely clear stored exec fields across affected channels.

recommendation.title: Make operator policy authoritative
recommendation.body: Have stricter operator/global exec policy win over stale stored session values, with a tested reset or migration path for existing entries.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the `/exec` session override behavior and added focused resolver coverage, so he is the best routing candidate for the policy choice.
